must_remember: Torricelli's Law states that the velocity of efflux of a liquid through an orifice at a depth $h$ below the free surface is $v = \sqrt{2gh}$.
The horizontal range of liquid efflux from an orifice at depth $h$ in a container of total height $H$ is given by $R = 2\sqrt{h(H - h)}$, reaching its maximum when $h = H/2$.
A Venturi meter measures the volume flow rate of incompressible fluids by creating a pressure differential via a constricted throat.
The Magnus effect describes the transverse force on a spinning body moving through a fluid due to circulation and asymmetrical pressure distribution.
Bernoulli's equation $P + \frac{1}{2}\rho v^2 + \rho gz = \text{constant}$ is a restatement of the work-energy theorem for ideal, steady, streamline, incompressible fluid flow.

glossary.meaning: A device utilizing Bernoulli's principle to measure fluid flow rate through pipes by employing a converging section and a narrow throat.
A relation stating that fluid efflux velocity from an orifice equals the speed acquired by a body falling freely from the fluid surface to the orifice depth.
The generation of a transverse aerodynamic lift force on a spinning cylinder or sphere moving through a fluid.
The static pressure plus dynamic pressure at a stagnation point where fluid velocity is brought to zero, measured by a Pitot tube.
The line integral of the fluid velocity vector around a closed curve enclosing a lifting body, central to lift generation in aerodynamics.
